newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Support for Argentina's Menem lingers at 17% - poll.
newsitem.headline: Support for Argentina's Menem lingers at 17% - poll.

text.p: Support for Argentine President Carlos Menem has increased slightly but remains low, with 17 percent prepared to vote for him if he ran in 1999 elections, according to an opinion poll published on Tuesday.
The survey of 600 people, conducted last month by Market & Opinion Research International (MORI), shows support increased from 11 percent last October and nine percent in February.
The Peronist president is banned by law from running for a third term in office in 1999 presidential polls, and has denied persistent speculation he may find a way to run again.

The modest increase in support, Mori said, was due to "a certain improvement in the perception of the country's economic situation." The government has forecast that the economy will grow by five percent this year and unemployment will fall from the 17 percent level last year.

The survey indicated that those who disapprove of the government's free market economic policies fell to 70 percent from 72 percent in February, while approval for the policies rose to 18 percent from 15 percent.

Support for Buenos Aires province Governor Eduardo Duhalde, a Peronist tipped as the most likely successor of Menem at the presidency, increased to 40 percent from 37 percent in February but was still down from 49 percent last October.
The backing of Buenos Aires city Mayor Fernando de la Rua, of the Radical Party, rose to 35 percent from 29 percent in February.
